meta.title: Foyer
meta.description: Set rules for your AI assistants so they don’t spend or book without agreement.

home.title: Keep your AI assistants from fighting over your money.
home.lead: One bot books travel. Another watches the budget. They both act in your name, but they want different things. You write the rules. Foyer checks each request against those rules before anything is paid or booked.

wizard.rulesTitle: A few questions, then you can edit the text.
wizard.rulesLead: Assistants will read this text — not the questionnaire.
wizard.qPrice: If a trip can be cheaper or more comfortable, what should win?
wizard.qPromises: If something was already promised to someone outside, does that beat an internal change of plans?
wizard.qSecurity: May a security assistant block email that looks like a payment or other people’s data?
wizard.qLegal: Should Legal block a delivery date that is wider than the contract?
wizard.qFinance: May finance block a spend over the monthly limit?
wizard.qHumanPlaceholder: For example: if the amount is large or the rule is unclear
wizard.lockTitle: What has to go through these rules?
wizard.lockLead: Unchecked items are not available to assistants here.
wizard.guardianLead: Budget, calendar, and security stay here. They object when the rules say so.
wizard.guardianLeadOrg: They stay here. Legal watches promises. Finance watches spend.
wizard.firstLead: Three requests: a €420 ticket, moving a promised call, and a spreadsheet with emails. You should see them in the list.
wizard.firstLeadOrg: Sales will promise a Friday delivery. Legal can object.

charter.spend: Do not spend more than {limit} per month without a separate decision.
charter.save: Save money, except being late for work or losing a client.
charter.balance: Balance price and comfort. Prefer the cheaper option unless time or a client is at risk.
charter.comfort: Comfort may win over price when the trip is for work.
charter.promisesNo: An internal schedule may change an external promise if the cost is high.
charter.securityYes: Security may block mail that looks like payment or other people's data.
charter.securityNo: Security does not veto ordinary mail.
charter.orgLegal: Do not promise a client a deadline wider than the contract.
charter.orgFinance: Finance may block spend over the monthly limit.

outline.constitutionLead: You write what is allowed. Every assistant follows the same text. The court reads it too.
outline.gatewayLead: An assistant cannot pay, book, or message the outside world on its own. It asks through Foyer. If nobody objects, it goes through.
outline.courtLead: If they disagree, the court decides: go ahead, block it, find a middle, or ask you. If it cannot decide, you decide. You can appeal.

check.title: How to test
check.lead: Walk this list on the public URL. The product is the cabinet, not spawn.
items: A person without OpenAPI can connect an assistant in a few copy-pastes.
With one own assistant, a dispute still appears (guardian).
The dispute goes through agent calls, not “I am budget” clicks.
All four outcomes show up, including allow_b as a counter and as a pure block.
A remedy verdict executes from remedy_action, without a human reading prose.
An untouched request still resolves when nobody pokes the app (the tick).
There is execution (at least a stub) and appeal.
A live house can show an on-chain tx when consensus lands.
Spawn does not pass itself off as the product.
The public URL keeps state after a reload.
Someone else’s house stays invisible without its agent key or the owner’s wallet.

protocol.title: For developers
protocol.lead: Each assistant gets its own key and talks to Foyer only with that key.
